blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Diffusion language models (DLMs) support parallel generation, yet they often require many denoising steps because only a fraction of token predictions are sufficiently reliable to be committed at each step. Existing acceleration methods primarily optimize confidence learning or commitment policies. However, these approaches operate on the outputs of a single denoising forward pass, in which information from the prompt, previously committed tokens, and uncommitted positions may not yet be fully integrated. Consequently, some predictions remain under-refined when the commitment decision is made, and modifying the commitment policy alone cannot improve their underlying representations. We introduce dLoop, which restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a Prelude-Loop-Coda architecture and recurrently applies a parameter-shared intermediate block to the same partially masked state. Rather than advancing the denoising process, each additional loop provides further latent computation, allowing information distributed across uncommitted positions to continue interacting and become more fully integrated before commitment. Experiments on GSM8K, MATH, MBPP, and HumanEval show that dLoop achieves the highest or tied-highest accuracy on every benchmark. With tokens per forward pass (TPF) adjusted for loop computation, it outperforms Fast-dLLM in both accuracy and TPF on all four benchmarks and dParallel on three, and is more accurate than d3LLM on all four, while d3LLM attains higher TPF; no compared method surpasses dLoop in both. Mechanistic analyses show that extra loops mainly help on slow, unstable trajectories and that updates at uncommitted positions drive changes in token decisions and later generation. Pre-commitment latent computation thus makes predictions more reliable, offering a route to DLM acceleration distinct from forcing confidence through the training loss.
blocks.zh: 扩散语言模型(DLMs)支持平行生成,然而它们往往需要许多去名步骤,因为只有一小部分的符号预测足够可靠,可以在每个步骤上承诺. 现有的加速方法主要是优化信心学习或承诺政策。 然而,这些办法依靠的是单一取消前期通行证的产出,在该通行证中,来自迅速、先前承诺的标志和未承诺立场的信息可能尚未充分整合。 因此,在作出承诺决定时,有些预测仍然不够完善,仅修改承诺政策并不能改善它们的基本表述。 我们引入dLoop,它将一个预先训练的传播语言模型重组为Prelude-Loop-Coda架构,并反复将一个参数共享的中间块应用到同一个部分遮掩状态. 每个额外的循环不是推进解密进程,而是提供进一步的潜伏计算,使分布在未承诺位置上的信息能够继续互动,并在承诺之前更加全面整合。 在GSM8K,MATH,MBPP,和HumanEval上的实验显示,dLoop在每个基准上都实现了最高或捆绑最高的精度. 每一次前传的令牌(TPF)经过调整以进行循环计算后,它在所有四个基准的精确度和TPF的精确度上都超过了快速dLLLM,在三个基准上都超过了dParallel,而且在所有四个基准上都比d3LLLM更准确,而d3LLLM则获得更高的TPF;在这两个基准上,没有比比方法都超过dLoop. 机械分析显示,额外的循环主要有助于缓慢、不稳定的轨迹,在非承诺位置更新会推动象征性决定和后世的改变。 因此,承诺前的潜在计算使预测更加可靠,为DLM加速提供了一条与通过培训损失而强迫信任不同的路径。

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Diffusion language models (DLMs) progressively resolve masked tokens through
iterative denoising, providing a parallel alternative to left-to-right
autoregressive decoding ( Nie et al. 2025 ) . By predicting multiple positions
in one forward pass, DLMs have the potential for parallel generation.
High-quality generation, however, often requires many denoising steps because
only a subset of predictions is reliable enough to commit at each step.
Enabling more predictions to become reliable in fewer steps without
sacrificing generation quality is therefore central to efficient DLM
inference.

Existing acceleration methods primarily improve token commitment through
training or decoding. dParallel uses certainty-forcing distillation to make
correct masked-token predictions reach high confidence earlier ( Chen et al. 2025 ) , and d3LLM retains this certainty-forcing loss while
adding pseudo-trajectory distillation and entropy-guided multi-block decoding ( Qian et al. 2026 ) . Fast-dLLM combines confidence-aware parallel decoding
with approximate KV caching to increase parallel commitment and reduce the
cost of repeated denoising ( Wu et al. 2025 ) . Other approaches use
confidence estimation, local commitment windows, or decoding schedules to
determine when and which predictions should be finalized. These methods mainly
improve when predictions become commit-ready, when tokens are committed, or
the cost of repeated denoising.

Nevertheless, some predictions may remain immature when the decoder must make
a commitment decision. The decoder can commit or defer them, but cannot
further improve the representations from which they were formed. When many
positions remain masked, information relevant to a prediction is distributed
across the prompt, committed positions, and other uncommitted representations ( He et al. 2026 ) , and may not be fully propagated in one forward pass.
Rather than only optimizing how existing predictions are committed, we ask a
complementary question: can a model continue computing before irreversible
commitment, allowing immature predictions to be further refined into more
reliable token distributions?

blocks.en:
Recurrent-depth models provide a natural mechanism for this purpose.
Repeatedly executing parameter-shared Transformer layers before producing an
output allows hidden states to evolve in continuous latent space, expanding
test-time computation without generating additional external tokens ( Geiping et al. 2025 ; McLeish et al. 2025 ; Prairie et al. 2026 ) . This
process can be viewed as latent computation: the model iteratively processes
its internal representations before mapping the resulting state to a token
prediction. Recent work applies recurrence to masked diffusion models and
demonstrates benefits from increased loop depth ( Lee et al. 2026 ) .
However, how such pre-commitment computation changes uncommitted
representations and subsequently affects token commitment remains
insufficiently understood.

blocks.en:
Motivated by this perspective, we introduce dLoop, which performs recurrent
latent computation within each denoising step before commitment. The model
keeps the current partially masked state unchanged and repeatedly executes a
parameter-shared intermediate block. Extra loops neither reveal new tokens nor
advance to a new external denoising step; instead, they allow the hidden
representations of uncommitted positions to continue evolving and interacting.
Only after these extra passes does the model produce the predictions used for
commitment. Increasing recurrent depth is therefore not an end in itself, but
a mechanism for further refining immature predictions before they become
fixed context.

blocks.en:
Starting from a pretrained LLaDA checkpoint, we instantiate dLoop using a
Prelude–Loop–Coda architecture and adapt it through supervised fine-tuning.
The Prelude encodes the current partially masked sequence, the parameter-shared
Loop Block performs one or more additional passes over the same state, and the
Coda maps the updated representations to token distributions. No token is
committed and the model does not advance to a new denoising state during an
extra loop. A confidence-aware decoder then converts predictions satisfying
the commitment criterion into parallel commitments.

blocks.en:
We evaluate dLoop against Fast-dLLM, dParallel, and d3LLM on GSM8K, MATH,
MBPP, and HumanEval, using task accuracy and tokens per forward pass (TPF)
with the computation of extra loops included. dLoop achieves the highest or
tied-highest accuracy on every benchmark, and no compared method surpasses it
in both accuracy and TPF. Unlike dParallel and d3LLM, which push predictions
to become confident earlier through a certainty-forcing loss, dLoop keeps the
standard masked-token cross-entropy and lets confidence rise through
additional computation before commitment. This demonstrates that
pre-commitment latent computation offers an effective acceleration route
distinct from confidence training, cache optimization, and commitment
scheduling.

blocks.en:
We further analyze how extra loops affect internal states and subsequent
generation. Extra loops primarily act on slow and unstable generation
trajectories. Hidden-state and attention analyses show that uncommitted
representations are reorganized and locally reselect salient attention
connections during the additional computation. Source-rollback interventions
further identify their joint update as the main source of changes in token
candidates and commitment decisions. The unchanged Coda then maps these
refined representations to new token distributions; newly committed tokens
become context for later denoising steps and alter the subsequent trajectory.
These analyses connect recurrent latent computation and distributed
refinement of uncommitted representations to token commitment and complete
generation.

Our contributions are threefold: 1. We introduce dLoop, which adds recurrent latent computation for
immature predictions before irreversible token commitment without
creating a new external denoising state. 2. We show across four reasoning and code-generation benchmarks that

a highly competitive accuracy–parallelism trade-off against Fast-dLLM,
dParallel, and d3LLM. 3. We provide a mechanistic analysis showing how extra loops reorganize
uncommitted representations, change token candidates and commitment
decisions, and ultimately affect subsequent generation.

blocks.en:
Diffusion language models replace a fixed left-to-right factorization with iterative prediction over masked positions, enabling flexible generation orders and multi-token commitment ( Nie et al. 2025 ) .
Their practical speed is nevertheless governed by an accuracy–parallelism trade-off: aggressive commitment reduces denoising steps but can turn immature predictions into irreversible context.
Existing work improves this trade-off by changing either the training objective or the decoding policy.
dParallel uses certainty-forcing distillation to accelerate certainty convergence across masked positions ( Chen et al. 2025 ) , whereas d3LLM combines pseudo-trajectory distillation with entropy-guided multi-block decoding and cache refresh ( Qian et al. 2026 ) .
Training-free approaches instead modify inference: Fast-dLLM combines confidence-aware parallel decoding with approximate KV caching ( Wu et al. 2025 ) , while Deferred Commitment Decoding uses a confidence-aware sliding window to postpone uncertain decisions ( Shu et al. 2026 ) .
Together, these methods accelerate diffusion decoding either by making more tokens ready for earlier commitment or by reducing the cost of repeated denoising.

传播语言模型用被遮住的位置的迭代预测取代了固定的左向右的分化,从而能够灵活生成命令和多托肯承诺(Nie等人,2025年)。
然而,它们的实际速度受到精确性 — — 平行性权衡的制约:侵略性承诺会减少虚名步骤,但可将不成熟的预测变成不可逆转的背景。
现有工作通过改变培训目标或解码政策来改进这种取舍。
dParallel 使用确定性强化蒸馏来加速不同被遮蔽位置的确定性趋同 (Chen等人,2025年),而d3LLM结合了伪导出物蒸馏和肽-导多块解码和缓存刷新(Qian等人,2026年).
非培训性办法修改了推断: 快报d LLM将信心意识平行解码与大约KV caching(Wu等2025年)相结合,而延迟承诺解码则使用信心感滑动窗口来推迟不确定的决定(Shu等2026年).
这些方法加在一起,通过使更多的信使为更早的承诺做好准备来加快传播解码工作,或者通过减少重复去名的费用来加速传播。

blocks.en:
Recurrent and looped Transformers repeatedly apply a parameter-shared block, allowing test-time computation to vary without duplicating its parameters.
Recurrent-depth models establish this mechanism as a latent test-time-compute axis ( Geiping et al. 2025 ) , while Retrofitted Recurrence develops a training procedure for converting pretrained fixed-depth language models into recurrent ones ( McLeish et al. 2025 ) .
Parcae studies the stability and scaling behavior of looped residual dynamics and introduces a constrained input-injection mechanism ( Prairie et al. 2026 ) .
Other work explores how loop depth should be allocated: LoopFormer learns representations across variable-length recurrent trajectories ( Jeddi et al. 2026 ) , whereas Think-at-Hard selectively applies additional latent iterations to difficult token predictions ( Fu et al. 2025 ) .
Mechanistic analysis of looped autoregressive models identifies cyclic fixed-point behavior, attention stabilization, and repeated stages of inference across recurrent depth ( Blayney et al. 2026 ) .
Most directly for diffusion language modeling, LoopMDM applies selective looping to early–middle layers of masked diffusion models and demonstrates training- and inference-depth scaling, adaptive stopping, and increased interaction among masked positions ( Lee et al. 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
经常和循环的变形器反复应用一个参数共享块,允许测试时间的计算变化而不重复其参数.
经常性深入模式将这一机制确立为潜在的测试时间计算轴(Geiping等人,2025年),而再适应再现则制定将预先训练的固定深入语言模式转化为经常性语言模式的培训程序(McLeish等人,2025年)。
Parcae研究了循环残余动力学的稳定性和缩放行为,并引入了受约束的输入-注入机制(Prairie等,2026年).
其他工作探讨如何分配回路深度: LoopFormer学习跨可变长的经常性轨迹的表示(Jeddi等人,2026年),而 有选择地将额外的潜在迭代用于困难的符号预测(Fu等人,2025年)。
对循环自递性模型的机械分析确定了循环固定点行为,注意力稳定,以及跨反复深度反复推论的阶段(Blayney等,2026年).
LoopMDM最直接地用于传播语言模型,将选择性循环应用到早期-中层的蒙面传播模型中,并展示培训和推论深度的缩放、适应性停止和被蒙面位置之间更大的相互作用(Lee等,2026年)。

blocks.en:
Reasoning with Latent Tokens shows that still-masked positions are not computationally empty: their evolving predictions can support decisions elsewhere, and varying their number produces a speed–quality trade-off ( He et al. 2026 ) .
Latent Refinement Decoding approaches the same broad issue from decoding, treating premature commitment as information loss and retaining distributional beliefs across denoising steps ( Zhu et al. 2025 ) .
Together, these studies motivate viewing uncommitted positions as an evolving latent workspace rather than as empty placeholders awaiting prediction.

改进 解码从解码到处理同样的广泛问题,将过早承诺视为信息损失,并保留不同解码步骤的分配信仰(Zhu等人,2025年)。
这些研究共同促使人们将未承诺的立场视为一个不断变化的潜在工作空间,而不是等待预测的空位。

blocks.en:
Prior work separately establishes efficient token commitment, recurrent depth as an internal compute axis, and the latent representations carried by uncommitted positions.
dLoop connects these directions by placing trained recurrent computation before token commitment and tracing how updates to the uncommitted latent workspace change confidence, commitment decisions, and subsequent denoising.

At each denoising step, dLoop refines the current partially masked state
through recurrent computation before the decoder commits tokens. We next
describe its recurrent architecture, multi-depth training, and decoding
procedure.

blocks.en:
We divide LLaDA ( Nie et al. 2025 ) into three consecutive
functional components: a Prelude that encodes the current partially masked
sequence, a parameter-shared Loop Block that performs repeated computation,
and a Coda that reads the updated representations and produces token
predictions. Inspired by recurrent-depth architectures ( Geiping et al. 2025 ; McLeish et al. 2025 ) , we use a consecutive
group of intermediate layers as the repeatable computation block: layers
0–15 form the Prelude, layers 16–21 form the Loop Block, and layers 22–31
form the Coda. Figure 1 illustrates this architecture and
the recurrent computation performed within each denoising step.

blocks.en:
All experiments build on LLaDA. dLoop uses the recurrent architecture described in
the Method section, with layers 16–21 serving as the parameter-shared Loop
Block. At inference time, we use the confidence-aware decoder described in
the Method section to commit mature predictions within a moving local window.
We evaluate mathematical reasoning on GSM8K and MATH, and code generation on
MBPP and HumanEval. We compare with native LLaDA, Fast-dLLM ( Wu et al. 2025 ) , dParallel ( Chen et al. 2025 ) , and d3LLM ( Qian et al. 2026 ) . Training details are given in the appendix.

blocks.en:
This split between accuracy and TPF reflects the trade-off between accuracy
and parallelism in decoding acceleration, and it stems from how the two kinds
of methods raise prediction confidence. dParallel and d3LLM work through the
loss: a certainty-forcing loss directly pushes predictions to become
confident earlier, so that more tokens can be committed per step; d3LLM
builds further optimizations on dParallel while keeping the same core idea.
dLoop instead works through the model structure: its loss remains the
standard masked-token cross-entropy, with no confidence-specific term in the
training objective, and it adds a recurrent loop block so that predictions
receive additional computation before commitment. Confidence then rises
spontaneously through this additional latent computation, allowing
predictions to mature faster and thereby also accelerating decoding. The two
routes therefore emphasize different goals. Forcing confidence through the
loss favors parallelism, and together with the further optimizations of
d3LLM, this gives d3LLM the highest TPF. Letting confidence mature through
the structure favors accuracy, while the extra computation of the loops is
fully counted in adjusted TPF, so dLoop does not reach the TPF of d3LLM.
Taken together, on every benchmark in Table 1 , no other
method achieves both higher accuracy and higher TPF than dLoop. dLoop is
thus a highly competitive choice on the accuracy–parallelism trade-off, and
it represents a route to DLM acceleration distinct from dParallel and d3LLM.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced dLoop, which uses recurrent latent computation to refine
immature predictions before irreversible token commitment. By repeatedly
executing a parameter-shared intermediate block on the same partially masked
state, dLoop extends internal processing without advancing to a new
denoising step. Across four reasoning and code-generation benchmarks, it
achieves the highest or tied-highest accuracy on every benchmark, and no
compared method, including Fast-dLLM, dParallel, and d3LLM, surpasses it in
both accuracy and TPF. Unlike methods that force confidence through the
training loss, dLoop lets confidence rise through additional computation
before commitment, offering a distinct route to DLM acceleration. Our
analyses show that extra loops perform distributed latent refinement by
reorganizing uncommitted representations and locally reselecting salient
context. These changes alter the leading candidate and its separation from
alternatives, affect commitment decisions, and propagate through subsequent
denoising, connecting pre-commitment latent refinement to the observed
accuracy–parallelism improvements.

blocks.en:
An autoregressive model generates one token per forward pass, whereas a
diffusion language model can commit several tokens in a single forward pass.
Work on diffusion language models therefore commonly measures decoding
parallelism by TPF: the number of generated tokens divided by the number of
forward passes.

The assumption holds for LLaDA, Fast-dLLM, dParallel, and d3LLM, each of

dLoop is different: a step with k k extra loops reruns the 6 loop layers of

i.e., 1.188, 1.375, and 1.563 for k = 1 , 2 , 3 k=1,2,3 .

computation spent in each step.

TPF is not itself a measure of time, but it is closely related to time: the
time to solve a problem equals the number of denoising steps multiplied by

For the same model and implementation, the time per step is roughly constant,

Each dLoop step becomes slower because of the extra loops, and adjusted TPF

layers executed.
As long as the time per step grows in proportion to the number of layers
executed, adjusted TPF agrees with the actual time.
